answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained work: an agent must build a verifiable history of useful contributions before it gains voting weight, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities buys nothing. Think of reputation as a glacier — it moves slowly and grows only through steady, observable effort over time. A newcomer starts with a tiny delta of trust and earns more by completing real tasks, while an opal-grade credential, issued only after verified milestones, unlocks higher privileges. Sybils can copy code, but they cannot fake months of attested work.
